payload.bug: system-auditor mislabels the weekday in its audit summary
payload.evidence: 3+ consecutive runs wrong: tier-1 (prior) wrote 'Today is Sunday' for 2026-06-09; tier-2 used 'Tuesday' only after explicit router correction in the spawn prompt; tier-1 (this run) wrote '2026-06-08 = Saturday'. Ground truth via `date -j -f %Y-%m-%d`: 2026-06-08 = Monday (Lundi), 2026-06-09 = Tuesday (Mardi). The Saturday label is off by 2 days even with the correct date supplied in the prompt.
payload.impact: Cosmetic so far — Tier-1/2 ran date-agnostic, no weekday-gated check fired. RISK: any trading-day or weekday-gated auditor check (or downstream consumer reading the summary) would false-positive. Mirrors the tran-ngoc-bau F-SUNDAY false-CRITICAL class of bug.
payload.root_cause_hypothesis: Weekday is inferred/guessed by the model rather than derived from a real clock call. Fix: in the auditor flow, compute weekday strictly from `date -u +%A` (and local `date +%A`) and echo both into the summary; never let the model name the day from memory.
payload.suggested_owner: agent-father — edit the auditor flow weekday/summary step. Invoke the agent-md-factory skill first (SSOT/DRY) per project rule before editing the agent .md.
payload.verification_gate: next 2 auditor runs print a weekday that matches `date +%A` on the run host
